findings.title: User-storage write payload cannot be read back as a recovery-code credential
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential tells user storage to persist only a JSON array of the raw recovery codes (UserCredentialModel challenge response). It drops generatedAt, the user label, and the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel that createFromValues already built. RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator then take the first federated credential of this type and pass it to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel, which requires secretData in Keycloak's hashed schema. A provider that stores the updateCredential value and returns that CredentialModel (secretData null, credentialData = the raw JSON) — the same shape this PR's test storage saves, and the same pattern used for OTP — makes the login form throw while parsing, or throws after isValid already accepted the code, so recovery-code login never completes. Only the test provider papers over this by ignoring the stored model and calling createFromValues inside getCredentials.

findings.title: Used federated recovery codes are not consumed or deleted
findings.body: After credentialManager().isValid succeeds, this authenticator assumes the credential row was already updated and, when allCodesUsed() is true, deletes it with removeStoredCredentialById. That side effect exists only in the local recovery-code credential provider. For the new user-storage path, isValid is delegated to the storage provider and this method never writes the remaining codes back with updateCredential. removeStoredCredentialById only deletes credentials stored in Keycloak's database, not credentials owned by user storage, and the id on a federated model is not a local credential id. A correct storage that marks codes used therefore leaves an exhausted credential in place: isConfiguredFor stays true, the browser flow keeps challenging for a recovery code before required actions run, and the user is locked out once the last code is consumed. A storage that does not mutate state on isValid (as the new test provider does) leaves every code reusable forever, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES action is never added.

findings.title: Reference user storage accepts any recovery code forever and stores them in plaintext
findings.body: updateCredential saves input.getChallengeResponse() verbatim in credentialData, which is the JSON array of raw codes, not hashes. isValid then returns true if any stored code equals the input and does not remove the match or require it to be the next unused code. getCredentials ignores that stored model and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues on the original list, which assigns a new id and marks every code unused. So the code index shown at login never advances, allCodesUsed() is never true, removeStoredCredentialById cannot target the real id, and a captured code can be replayed indefinitely. testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only signs in once with code 0, so it does not catch replay, a stuck index, plaintext persistence, or failure to force regeneration.

findings.title: Recovery-code login form throws if the federated credential is missing or incomplete
findings.body: The constructor always calls credentialModelOpt.get() and RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel, then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). getCredential now prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream() over local storage. If that stream is empty (storage accepted updateCredential but does not implement getCredentials), if the model has no secretData, or if every code is already used, rendering the recovery-code page throws NoSuchElementException or a JSON error instead of a challenge. Previously this bean only read local credentials created by the credential provider, which always had the hashed schema and a remaining code when the form was shown.

findings.title: Recovery-codes feature is enabled without restarting the server
findings.body: @EnableFeature(RECOVERY_CODES, skipRestart = true) only flips the runtime profile flag. RecoveryAuthnCodesAction, the recovery-authn-codes credential provider, and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticatorFactory are environment-dependent factories whose isSupported() checks that feature and which are registered at server start. Without a restart they stay undeployed, so the new browser-flow execution and CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action do not run createRecoveryCodesCredential. The test can fail or not exercise the user-storage path at all. Omit skipRestart so the server restarts with the providers loaded.
